exposure: Delivery methods (assistive instruments like forceps or suction)
cohort: The study included children aged 0-15 years newly diagnosed with childhood brain tumors in Ontario, Canada, between 1997 and 2003.
finding: The use of assistive instruments (forceps or suction) during childbirth was significantly associated with an increased risk of overall CBTs and non-glial tumors, while second-born or greater children had a lower risk of overall CBT development compared to first-borns.
mod_finding: The use of assistive instruments (forceps or suction) during childbirth was significantly associated with an increased risk of overall childhood brain tumors.
